_note: Oracle vectors. Wire-format byte alignment (Elsys typed-TLV) is taken from reference/upstream-codec.js (DecodeElsysPayload); expected.data is the authored normalization to the shared vocabulary (action.contactState for a port's dry contact — the reed/door switch on port 1 — scoped into that port's `channels[]` entry, action.motion at the top level for the whole-device accelerometer movement count). Vector 1 uses the upstream TTN example input (ACC + PULSE1 + PULSE1_ABS: whole-device axes top-level, port-1 pulse counters in the `port0` entry, no door/motion fields present in that capture). Vectors 2-3 are synthetic door + motion captures; vector 4 exercises both external ports; vectors 5-6 are error inputs.

uplink.description: EMS Door accelerometer (raw X/Y/Z) top-level plus port 1 pulse counters
Door open (port 1 reed digital=1) with 3 movement events
Door closed (port 1 reed digital=0) with no movement
Both external ports populated: port 1 open contact + probe temperature, port 2 closed contact + probe temperature + pulse count
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds Elsys TLV frame exercising BOTH external ports with distinct values, including two quantities on each port. Raw decode confirmed via the ORACLE method against reference/upstream-codec.js: {motion:2, vdd:3600, externalTemperature:21, digital:1, pulse2:7, externalTemperature2:-2, digital2:0}. expected.data is the authored normalization: MOTION and VDD are whole-device (action.motion / battery = mV/1000, top-level); each port's dry contact maps to action.contactState inside that port's entry (digital!==0 -> open), and the port-2 probe/pulse readings use the same port-index-free key names as port 1.
